## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(maps)
```
```{r}
breeding_site_locations <- read_csv("data/breeding_site_locations.csv")
```


```{r}
gt(breeding_site_locations)
```
#enables us to view the data frame

```{r}
colnames(breeding_site_locations)
```
#shows column names from the data frame

```{r}
glimpse(breeding_site_locations)
```
#shows summary of the data frame
#includes number of rows and columns in the data frame

```{r}
print(nrow(breeding_site_locations))
print(ncol(breeding_site_locations))
print(dim(breeding_site_locations))
```
#used to print out number of rows, columns and both rows + columns, respectively
